name: mountupd
description:
mount(2)'s MNT_UPDATE ARM: read-only to read-write in place, which is what `mount -u' is and what a root fsck'd read-only at boot needs to become writable again.  /dev/sd1 is the scratch spindle (disk/ufsscratch.po via extra_hards) and /mnt an empty directory on the boot volume; ufsmount covers the plain mount and unmount on the same pair.

WHAT EACH MARKER DISCRIMINATES, and every one of them can go red alone:
  MUTYPE   mount(2) with a type that has no vfssw[] row -- MOUNT_NONE's null row, and MOUNT_MAXTYPE+1 past the table -- answered ENODEV, and the refusal left /mnt free: the UFS mount straight after it is the positive control, being the one row the table has.
  MUCREAT  a read-only mount REFUSED a create with EROFS.  This is the positive control: without it a mount that was writable all along would 'become' writable and every marker below would be vacuous.
  MUUPD    mount(2) with MNT_UPDATE returned 0.
  MUWROTE  a create SUCCEEDED afterwards.
  MUPERSIST the file and its bytes SURVIVED an unmount and a fresh mount.  This is the assertion and MUWROTE is not: reading back through the mount that created it answers from the in-core inode, so a write that never reached the platter reads correctly and corrupts nothing.  Measured -- without the round trip, deleting the update arm's sb_ronly line left this probe GREEN.
  MURO     read-write to read-only was REFUSED with ENOTSUP.  Both trees refuse that direction; allowing it would be inventing an interface.
  MUDONE   the unmount afterwards still works.

The `lacks' arms name the failure markers the probe prints instead: MUNOTRO (writable while read-only, the vacuity case), MUNORO (the refusal did not happen) and MUNOWRITE (the update did not actually make it writable).
